sections.heading: Key Takeaways
paragraphs: **Prioritize Your Health and the Evidence**: After an accident, see a doctor right away to officially link your injuries to the event. At the same time, gather as much proof as you can, including photos, witness information, and the police report, to build the strongest possible case.

**Know North Carolina's Unique Laws**: State-specific rules, like the strict contributory negligence doctrine, can completely determine your case's outcome. Understanding these laws is critical, as being found even 1% at fault could prevent you from recovering any compensation.

**You Can Afford Quality Legal Help**: Most personal injury lawyers work on a contingency fee basis, which means you pay no attorney fees unless they win your case. This structure removes the financial barrier, allowing you to seek justice without worrying about upfront costs.

sections.heading: Do I Have a Personal Injury Case in Charlotte?
paragraphs: If you’ve been hurt because of someone else’s actions or carelessness, you might be wondering about your next steps. Personal injury law is designed to help you recover from the harm you’ve suffered, but it can be hard to know if your situation qualifies. A personal injury case arises when you are injured due to another party's negligence. This can happen in many different ways, from a car crash on I-77 to a slip at a South End brewery. Understanding the most common types of claims is the first step in figuring out if you have a case.
Car and Motorcycle Accidents

Car and motorcycle accidents are a frequent cause of personal injury claims in Charlotte. If another driver’s negligence, like texting while driving or running a red light, caused your injuries, you likely have grounds for a claim. The key is proving that the other party was at fault and that their actions directly led to your physical harm and financial losses. After an accident, it's crucial to gather evidence and document your injuries to build a [valid personal injury claim](https://yalehaymondlaw.com/). This process helps ensure you can recover costs for medical bills, lost wages, and other damages.
Truck and Commercial Vehicle Accidents

Accidents involving large trucks or commercial vehicles are often devastating. Due to the sheer size and weight of these vehicles, collisions can result in catastrophic injuries and complex legal battles. These cases can involve multiple liable parties, including the driver, the trucking company, and even the vehicle manufacturer. If you've been in a crash with a commercial truck, understanding your rights is essential. An experienced legal team can investigate the accident to determine fault and fight for the full [potential for compensation](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) you deserve for your significant losses.
Slip and Fall Accidents

Property owners have a responsibility to keep their premises safe for visitors. When they fail to do so, and you get hurt as a result, it’s known as a slip and fall accident. These incidents can happen anywhere, from a wet floor in a grocery store to a broken step at an apartment complex. If you were injured because of an unsafe condition that the owner knew or should have known about, you may have a [case for premises liability](https://www.cvinjurylaw.com/). Documenting the hazardous condition and your injuries is vital for proving negligence.
On-the-Job Injuries

Getting injured at work can happen in any profession, not just physically demanding ones. When you're hurt while performing your job duties, your primary path to recovery is typically through workers' compensation. This system is designed to provide benefits for medical treatment and lost wages without having to prove your employer was at fault. However, in some situations, you might also have a personal injury claim against a third party. For example, if a faulty piece of equipment from another company caused your injury, you may be entitled to file a separate lawsuit in addition to receiving [workers' compensation](https://yalehaymondlaw.com/).
Medical Malpractice

We trust healthcare professionals with our well-being, but sometimes, they make mistakes. Medical malpractice happens when a doctor, nurse, or hospital provides care that falls below the accepted medical standard, causing a patient to suffer an injury or illness. These cases are incredibly complex and require a deep understanding of both law and medicine. Examples include surgical errors, misdiagnosis, or birth injuries. If you suspect you’ve been harmed by a medical provider’s negligence, it is critical to seek [legal advice](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) from a specialist in this area to evaluate your claim.
Wrongful Death Claims

Losing a loved one is a profound tragedy, and it’s even more difficult when their death was caused by someone else’s wrongful act or negligence. In these situations, North Carolina law allows the deceased person's family to file a wrongful death claim. This type of lawsuit seeks to hold the responsible party accountable and secure financial stability for the surviving family members. A successful claim can provide [compensation for the deceased's family](https://yalehaymondlaw.com/), covering funeral expenses, lost income, and the loss of companionship and support.

sections.heading: How North Carolina Law Affects Your PI Claim
paragraphs: Every personal injury case is unique, but they all operate within the framework of state law. In North Carolina, a few specific rules can dramatically influence a claim's outcome. Understanding these laws is the first step in building a strong case strategy, as they dictate everything from who can file a lawsuit to who is eligible for compensation. For personal injury firms, mastering these nuances is essential for managing claims successfully and securing fair outcomes for your clients. These key legal principles are the foundation upon which every successful Charlotte personal injury claim is built.
The Three-Year Filing Deadline

Time is of the essence when it comes to personal injury claims in North Carolina. The state imposes a strict statute of limitations, giving an injured person a **three-year window** from the date of the incident to [file a personal injury lawsuit](https://yalehaymondlaw.com/). If you miss this deadline, the court will almost certainly refuse to hear your case, and you will lose the right to seek compensation permanently. For the most tragic cases involving wrongful death, this window is even shorter, closing just **two years** from the date of the person's passing. It’s a critical timeline to be aware of, as it forms the absolute cutoff for a client's right to justice.
Contributory Negligence: A Critical Rule to Understand

North Carolina is one of the few states that still follows the harsh **contributory negligence** rule. In simple terms, this doctrine states that if an injured person is found to be even slightly at fault for the accident, even just 1%, they are completely barred from recovering any damages. This rule creates a high-stakes environment where the defendant’s insurance company will work hard to shift any amount of blame onto the victim. For this reason, a successful claim requires a thorough investigation that clearly establishes the other party’s total liability, leaving no room for the defense to assign fault.
Special Rules for Claims Against the Government

Suing a government body is not the same as suing a private citizen or company. When filing claims against government entities in North Carolina, whether it's the city of Charlotte or a state agency, a different set of rules applies. These cases often involve shorter deadlines for giving notice of the claim and have very specific procedural requirements that must be followed precisely. Failing to adhere to these unique protocols under the North Carolina Tort Claims Act can easily lead to a case being dismissed before it even gets started. It’s a complex area of law where knowing the specific administrative hurdles is key.
How NC's "At-Fault" Insurance System Works

North Carolina operates under an [at-fault insurance system](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/), which means the person who is legally responsible for causing an accident is also responsible for paying the damages. In a car accident, for example, the at-fault driver’s liability insurance is the primary source of compensation for the injured party’s medical bills, lost wages, and other losses. While this sounds straightforward, insurance companies are businesses focused on their bottom line. Their adjusters are trained to minimize payouts, which often complicates the claims process. Having a skilled negotiator on your side is invaluable for ensuring your client's rights are protected and they receive the full compensation they deserve.

sections.heading: How Is a Personal Injury Settlement Calculated?
paragraphs: Explaining to a client how their settlement is calculated is one of the most important conversations you’ll have. It’s a process that blends hard math with nuanced assessments of human suffering. Getting it right sets clear expectations and builds the trust necessary for a strong attorney-client relationship. When your firm is powered by a steady stream of qualified cases from a service like [MVAMATCH](https://www.mvamatch.com), you have more time to dedicate to these crucial client conversations, ensuring they understand every step. A final settlement isn't just one number; it's a careful combination of several distinct components, each requiring its own method of valuation. Breaking down the calculation into economic damages, non-economic damages, and potential punitive damages helps demystify the process for your clients and grounds their expectations in reality. It also highlights the significant impact of external factors, like medical liens, which can affect the final amount they receive.
Calculating Economic Damages

Think of economic damages as the black-and-white, tangible losses that come with a paper trail. These are the most straightforward part of any settlement calculation because they represent actual money your client has lost or will lose due to their injury. We're talking about all documented medical expenses, from the initial emergency room visit and surgery to future costs for things like physical therapy and rehabilitation. This category also includes lost wages for any time your client was unable to work. It even covers out-of-pocket costs for services they now need to hire, like lawn care or childcare, that they could previously handle themselves. Meticulously documenting these expenses is non-negotiable for building a strong claim.
Valuing Non-Economic Damages

This is where the art of legal practice comes into play. Non-economic damages compensate your client for the intangible, human cost of their injury. There’s no receipt for pain and suffering, emotional distress, or the loss of enjoyment of life, yet these are often the most significant consequences of an accident. Valuing these damages requires experience and a deep understanding of how an injury has truly impacted a client's world. For example, even with a $50,000 settlement, after accounting for attorney’s fees, case costs, and outstanding medical bills, a client’s final take-home amount might be closer to half of that. Clearly explaining how these abstract losses are assigned a monetary value is key to managing client expectations.
When Are Punitive Damages Awarded?

It’s important to clarify with clients that punitive damages are rare and reserved for very specific circumstances. Unlike economic and non-economic damages, which are meant to compensate the victim, punitive damages are designed to punish the defendant. They are awarded when the at-fault party’s behavior was particularly reckless or malicious, such as in cases involving a drunk driver with a history of DUIs. The goal is to make an example of the wrongdoer and deter similar conduct in the future. In North Carolina, there are specific laws and caps that apply to punitive damages, so they are not a factor in most personal injury claims but can be significant when awarded.
How Medical Liens Impact Your Final Payout

One of the biggest surprises for clients can be the impact of medical liens on their settlement. A lien is a legal claim for payment against the settlement proceeds. If your client’s medical bills were paid by a health insurance company, Medicare, or Medicaid, that entity has a right to be reimbursed from the settlement. Hospitals and doctors who provided treatment on a lien basis also need to be paid back. These claims can significantly reduce the net amount your client receives. A crucial part of your job is not only identifying all potential liens but also negotiating them down to maximize the money that ultimately goes into your client's pocket.

sections.heading: The Personal Injury Claim Process, Step by Step
paragraphs: Understanding the personal injury claim process is the first step toward managing client expectations and building a strong case. While the details of every accident are different, the legal journey generally follows a clear, five-step path. From the moment an accident occurs to the final resolution, each phase has a distinct purpose and set of challenges. Knowing this roadmap helps you guide your clients with confidence, ensuring no critical detail is overlooked.

This structured approach allows you to methodically build your case, starting with the immediate preservation of evidence and moving through investigation, negotiation, and the ultimate decision between a settlement and a trial. For law firms aiming to scale, having a streamlined and repeatable process is key. When your intake team and legal staff understand these steps, you can handle a higher case volume efficiently without sacrificing the quality of representation for each client. This is how successful firms consistently achieve favorable outcomes. It transforms the complex legal dance into a series of manageable, predictable actions. This systemization is not about removing the human element; it's about creating the space for your team to focus on high-value tasks, like client strategy and negotiation, instead of getting bogged down by procedural chaos.
Step 1: Preserve Evidence Immediately

The moments right after an accident are the most critical for gathering evidence. You must advise your clients to act quickly, as evidence can disappear, memories can fade, and the scene can be altered. The foundation of any successful personal injury claim is built on strong, well-preserved proof of what happened. This includes taking photos and videos of the accident scene, the vehicles involved, and any visible injuries.

It's also essential to collect contact information from any witnesses and obtain a copy of the official police report. Furthermore, clients should keep a detailed file of all medical treatments, bills, and receipts related to their injuries. This initial collection of evidence is not just a preliminary task; it’s the raw material your firm will use to establish liability and prove the full extent of your client's damages.
Step 2: File Your Claim

Once your client has sought medical attention and you've gathered initial evidence, the next step is to formally file the claim. In North Carolina, there is a strict timeline for taking legal action. You generally have three years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. This rule, known as the statute of limitations, is a hard deadline. If you miss it, your client loses their right to seek compensation through the courts.

While three years may seem like a long time, it's crucial to begin the process much sooner. A thorough investigation and negotiation take time. Filing the claim officially notifies the at-fault party and their insurance company that you are seeking compensation on your client's behalf. This action formally opens the lines of communication and sets the stage for the negotiation phase to come.
Step 3: The Investigation and Evidence-Gathering Phase

This is where your legal team’s expertise truly comes into play. Your firm will conduct a deep and thorough investigation to uncover exactly how the accident occurred and who is legally responsible. This goes far beyond the initial evidence collection. It involves interviewing witnesses, consulting with accident reconstruction experts, obtaining medical records, and calculating the full scope of your client's economic and non-economic damages.

This phase is about building a compelling narrative backed by indisputable facts. Law firms that manage a consistent flow of cases often develop highly effective investigation systems. By partnering with services that help [grow your caseload](https://www.mvamatch.com), you can refine these internal processes, allowing your team to build powerful arguments that give your clients a significant advantage when it's time to negotiate.
Step 4: Negotiate with the Insurance Company

Negotiating with an insurance company is a delicate and often challenging process. Insurance adjusters are trained to protect their company's bottom line, which means their goal is to pay out as little as possible. Their initial settlement offers are almost always far below what your client truly deserves. Your role is to counter these lowball offers with a strong, evidence-based argument.

This is done by presenting a formal demand letter that details the facts of the case, establishes clear liability, and provides a comprehensive calculation of your client's damages. This includes medical bills, lost wages, and pain and suffering. The negotiation is a strategic back-and-forth, and your ability to demonstrate the strength of your case and your willingness to go to trial is what will compel the insurer to offer a fair settlement.
Step 5: Decide Between a Settlement or Trial

The vast majority of personal injury cases are resolved through a settlement. However, the final decision to accept an offer or take the case to trial rests with your client, guided by your expert advice. A settlement provides a guaranteed outcome and avoids the time, expense, and uncertainty of a trial. Your goal is to secure a settlement that is fair, but you must also be prepared to litigate if the insurance company refuses to negotiate in good faith.

This decision is especially critical in North Carolina due to the state's strict contributory negligence rule. If a jury finds your client even 1% at fault for the accident, they can be barred from recovering any compensation at all. This high-stakes rule makes your assessment of the case's strengths and weaknesses invaluable in helping your client decide whether to accept a final offer or risk going to court.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes That Can Weaken Your Personal Injury Claim
paragraphs: After an accident, it’s easy to make a misstep that could hurt your ability to get fair compensation. Knowing what to avoid is just as important as knowing what to do. When you’re recovering from an injury, the last thing you need is to jeopardize your claim without realizing it. Here are a few common mistakes that can unfortunately weaken a personal injury case, and how you can steer clear of them to protect your rights.
Mistake #1: Delaying Medical Care

Even if you feel okay right after an accident, you should see a doctor as soon as possible. Adrenaline can mask pain, and some serious injuries don't show symptoms for hours or even days. Waiting to get checked out gives an insurance company an opportunity to argue that your injuries aren't serious or that they were caused by something else entirely. Seeking prompt medical attention is the best way to [establish a clear link](https://www.tremoulislaw.com/blog/5-things-you-should-never-say-or-keep-from-your-personal-injury-lawyer/) between the injury and the accident. This creates an official medical record that becomes a crucial piece of evidence for your claim and shows you took your health seriously from the start.
Mistake #2: Failing to Document Evidence

In the chaos following an accident, it can be hard to think clearly, but evidence is your best friend. If you are able, try to document everything you can. Use your phone to take pictures and videos of the accident scene, your injuries, and any property damage. Get the names and contact information of any witnesses. Once you’re home, start a simple journal to track your symptoms, medical appointments, and how the injury impacts your daily life. It is essential to [gather and preserve all relevant evidence](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) to build a strong foundation for your case and prove the facts when memories start to fade.
Mistake #3: Speaking to Insurance Adjusters Alone

Soon after an accident, you will likely get a call from the other party’s insurance adjuster. They may seem friendly and concerned, but their job is to protect their company’s bottom line by paying out as little as possible. They are trained to ask questions that could lead you to unintentionally hurt your claim. You are not required to give them a recorded statement. It’s best to politely decline and direct them to your attorney. A personal injury lawyer can [handle these conversations](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) for you, ensuring your rights are protected and you don't say anything that could be used against you later.
Mistake #4: Underestimating Your Claim's True Value

Many people make the mistake of accepting the first settlement offer from an insurance company because they need the money and don't realize what their claim is actually worth. A fair settlement should cover more than just your current medical bills. It should account for future medical treatments, lost wages from time off work, and any impact on your future earning capacity. It also includes compensation for your pain and suffering. A lawyer can help you understand [how much your case is truly worth](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) by calculating the full extent of your damages, ensuring you don't settle for less than you deserve.

sections.heading: Your First Legal Consultation: What to Expect
paragraphs: Walking into a law office for the first time can feel a little overwhelming, but your initial consultation is simply a conversation. Think of it as a two-way interview. You’ll get to tell your story and learn about your legal options, and the attorney will assess the details of your case to see how they can help. Most personal injury lawyers offer this first meeting for free, so you can get professional advice without any financial commitment. The goal is for you to leave with a clear understanding of your rights and a sense of whether the attorney is the right partner to guide you through the claims process.
What to Bring to Your First Meeting

To make the most of your meeting, a little preparation goes a long way. Before you go, try to [prepare for your free meeting](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) by gathering any documents related to your accident. This includes the police report, your medical records, photos or videos of the accident scene and your injuries, and any correspondence you’ve had with insurance companies. It’s also helpful to write down everything you remember about how the accident happened while it’s still fresh in your mind. Don’t worry if you don’t have everything; just bring what you can. A list of questions for the attorney is also a great idea, ensuring you cover all your concerns. This information gives the lawyer a solid foundation for evaluating your claim.
Key Questions to Ask Your Potential Attorney

Your consultation is your opportunity to interview the attorney and decide if their firm is the right fit for you. Come prepared with questions that help you understand their experience, process, and fee structure. Start with the basics: Have you handled cases like mine before? What is your track record? You should also ask about logistics, like who your main point of contact will be and how often you can expect updates. Finally, don’t hesitate to discuss fees. You can [ask your lawyer for a detailed breakdown](https://a1accidentlawyer.com/how-much-of-a-50k-settlement-will-i-get/) of all potential costs and deductions from your settlement. A trustworthy attorney will be transparent about their contingency fee and any other expenses involved.
What Happens After the Consultation?

If you and the attorney agree to move forward, you will sign a representation agreement. This document outlines the attorney-client relationship and the contingency fee arrangement, meaning you won't pay any legal fees unless you win your case. Once the agreement is signed, your legal team gets to work immediately. They will notify all relevant parties, including insurance companies, that they are now representing you. From that point on, they handle all communications, so you no longer have to speak with adjusters. Their primary goal is to build a strong case and [get a settlement for you](https://yalehaymondlaw.com/), but they are always ready to go to court if a fair agreement can’t be reached.

sections.heading: How Do Personal Injury Lawyers Get Paid?
paragraphs: One of the biggest concerns after an accident is how you’ll afford legal help. The good news is that most personal injury lawyers in Charlotte don’t require any upfront payment. Instead, they use a payment structure that makes quality legal representation accessible to everyone, regardless of their financial situation. This approach ensures your lawyer is focused on the same goal you are: securing the best possible outcome for your case. Understanding how this works from the start can help you feel more confident as you move forward with your claim.
How Contingency Fees Work

Personal injury lawyers typically work on a contingency fee basis. This simply means their payment is contingent, or dependent, on winning your case. If you receive a settlement or a favorable court verdict, your attorney receives a pre-agreed percentage of that amount as their fee. If they don’t win the case, you don’t owe them any attorney fees. This structure aligns your lawyer’s goals directly with yours. The percentage is clearly outlined in your agreement before any work begins, so there are no surprises. This model allows you to pursue justice without the stress of paying legal bills along the way.
"No Win, No Fee": What It Really Means

You’ve probably seen the phrase “no win, no fee” in advertisements. It’s the most straightforward way to describe the contingency fee agreement. You will not pay your attorney for their time or work unless they successfully recover money for you. This promise is central to personal injury law and is designed to remove the financial risk from your shoulders. Most firms also offer a free initial consultation to discuss your case and determine if you have a valid claim. This allows you to get professional advice and understand your options before making any commitments, ensuring you feel comfortable with the path forward.
Accounting for Additional Case Costs and Expenses

While the “no win, no fee” promise covers your attorney’s professional fees, it’s important to understand that every legal case comes with additional costs. These are the out-of-pocket expenses required to build and pursue your claim. Common examples include court filing fees, charges for obtaining medical records, and fees for expert witnesses who may need to testify. These case costs are separate from the attorney's fee. Typically, your law firm will cover these expenses upfront and then deduct them from the final settlement amount, along with any outstanding medical liens and the agreed-upon attorney’s fee, before you receive your final payout.

sections.heading: How to Choose the Right Charlotte Personal Injury Lawyer
paragraphs: Finding the right lawyer can feel like the most critical decision you'll make after an injury, and in many ways, it is. You're not just hiring a legal expert; you're choosing a partner who will guide you through a complex and stressful process. The right attorney can make all the difference in both your peace of mind and the outcome of your case. To make a confident choice, focus on their specific experience, legal knowledge, communication style, and local presence.
Review Their Track Record in Personal Injury

When you're vetting potential attorneys, their past performance is a strong indicator of their future success. Look for a firm with a proven history of handling cases like yours. For example, a firm that has [successfully assisted](https://demayolaw.com/charlotte/personal-injury-lawyer/) tens of thousands of clients and secured significant financial results demonstrates a deep level of competence. Don't be shy about asking for case results or testimonials. A lawyer who is proud of their work will be transparent about their track record, giving you the confidence that they can effectively manage your claim and fight for the compensation you deserve.
Verify Their Knowledge of North Carolina Law

Personal injury law varies significantly from state to state, so you need a lawyer who knows North Carolina's laws inside and out. For instance, NC has a strict [contributory negligence rule](https://yalehaymondlaw.com/), which can prevent you from recovering any damages if you are found even 1% at fault for the accident. An experienced local attorney will understand these nuances and how they apply to your case. They will also be up-to-date on the three-year statute of limitations for filing a lawsuit, ensuring you don't miss any critical deadlines that could jeopardize your claim.
Assess Their Communication Style and Availability

The legal process can be long and emotionally draining, so your lawyer's communication style matters. You want an advocate who is not only strong in the courtroom but also compassionate and responsive to your needs. A firm that promises to be [available 24/7](https://www.cvinjurylaw.com/) to take your call shows a real commitment to client support. During your initial consultation, pay attention to how they listen and answer your questions. You should feel heard, respected, and confident that you'll be kept informed every step of the way, rather than being left in the dark about your own case.
Why Local Representation Is a Major Advantage

Choosing a lawyer based in Charlotte offers a distinct strategic edge. [Local representation](https://www.cvinjurylaw.com/) means your attorney is familiar with the local court system, judges, and even the opposing counsel. These established relationships and firsthand knowledge of the local legal landscape can be invaluable when negotiating a settlement or preparing for trial. A Charlotte-based lawyer is invested in the community and dedicated to helping local residents secure the fair compensation they deserve. This hometown advantage provides a level of insight that an out-of-town attorney simply can't match.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
paragraphs: **What if I think I was partly at fault for the accident? Can I still have a case?**

This is a really important question, especially in North Carolina. Our state has a strict rule called contributory negligence. In short, it means if you are found to be even 1% responsible for the accident, you could be prevented from recovering any money at all. Because the stakes are so high, it's vital not to assume you were at fault. Insurance companies will try to use this rule against you, so you need an experienced lawyer to investigate the facts and build a case that shows the other party was entirely responsible.
**How long does a personal injury case usually take to resolve?**

There isn't a single timeline that fits every case, as it depends on many factors. A straightforward claim with clear evidence might settle in a few months. However, a more complex case, especially one involving serious injuries or a dispute over who is at fault, could take a year or even longer, particularly if it needs to go to trial. The goal is always to get you the best possible result, and sometimes that means being patient while your legal team builds a strong case and negotiates effectively on your behalf.
**How much does it really cost to hire a personal injury lawyer?**

This is a common worry, but the payment structure is designed to help you. Personal injury lawyers work on a contingency fee basis, which means you pay no attorney fees upfront. Your lawyer's fee is a percentage of the final settlement or award they win for you. If you don't win your case, you don't owe them a fee for their work. This "no win, no fee" model allows you to get expert legal help without any financial risk.
**The other driver's insurance company wants me to give a recorded statement. Should I do it?**

It is best to politely decline to give a recorded statement without your own lawyer present. The insurance adjuster may seem friendly, but their job is to minimize the amount their company has to pay. They are trained to ask questions in a way that might lead you to say something that could weaken your claim later. Your best move is to let your attorney handle all communications with the insurance companies to protect your rights.
**Can you tell me how much my personal injury case is worth?**

It's impossible to give an accurate number right away, and you should be cautious of any lawyer who promises a specific amount early on. The true value of your case depends on many details, including the severity of your injuries, the total of your medical bills and lost wages, and the impact on your quality of life. A thorough calculation requires a full investigation of the facts and documentation of all your losses. A good lawyer will first focus on understanding every detail before giving you a realistic assessment of what you may be able to recover.
